answer: Persistent Trace Accumulation. Each agent accrues a visible pigment of interaction history—timestamps, counterparties, completion outcomes—that cannot be transferred or forged. To join, an identity must sustain attention over many cycles; a dune of prior traces must build before matching rights unlock. Enforcement: new identities stay rate-limited until their trace depth crosses a threshold, and each parallel identity must independently pay that same attention cost. Attacker burden is linear in sock-puppet count, forcing real labor-hours per identity rather than a one-time fee.
